# IBM Db2

[https://www.ibm.com/products/db2](https://www.ibm.com/products/db2)

![](https://img.shields.io/badge/memtables-fallback-yellow?style=flat-square) ![](https://img.shields.io/badge/inputs-Db2 tables-blue?style=flat-square) ![](https://img.shields.io/badge/outputs-Db2 tables | CSV | pandas | Parquet | PyArrow-orange?style=flat-square)

## Install

Install Ibis and dependencies for the Db2 backend:

::: {.panel-tabset}

## `pip`

Install with the `db2` extra:

```{.bash}
pip install 'ibis-framework[db2]'
```

And connect:

```{.python}
import ibis

con = ibis.db2.connect()  # <1>
```

1. Adjust connection parameters as needed.

## `conda`

Install for Db2:

```{.bash}
conda install -c conda-forge ibis-db2
```

And connect:

```{.python}
import ibis

con = ibis.db2.connect()  # <1>
```

1. Adjust connection parameters as needed.

## `mamba`

Install for Db2:

```{.bash}
mamba install -c conda-forge ibis-db2
```

And connect:

```{.python}
import ibis

con = ibis.db2.connect()  # <1>
```

1. Adjust connection parameters as needed.

:::

## Connect

### `ibis.db2.connect`

```python
con = ibis.db2.connect(
    database="SAMPLE",
    host="localhost",
    port=50000,
    user="db2inst1",
    password="password",
    schema="MYSCHEMA",
)
```

::: {.callout-note}
`ibis.db2.connect` is a thin wrapper around [`ibis.backends.db2.Backend.do_connect`](#ibis.backends.db2.Backend.do_connect).
:::

### Connection Parameters

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _utils import render_do_connect

render_do_connect("db2")
```

### SSL connections

Use `ssl=True` to enable an encrypted connection (default Db2 SSL port: **50001**).
Set `ssl=False` (the default) for plain unencrypted connections.

```python
# Plain connection — ssl defaults to False
con = ibis.db2.connect(
    database="SAMPLE",
    host="db2-server.example.com",
    port=50000,
    user="db2inst1",
    password="password",
    ssl=False,
)

# SSL — no certificate validation (useful for self-signed certs in dev)
con = ibis.db2.connect(
    database="SAMPLE",
    host="db2-server.example.com",
    port=50001,
    user="db2inst1",
    password="password",
    ssl=True,
)

# SSL — with server certificate (recommended for production)
con = ibis.db2.connect(
    database="SAMPLE",
    host="db2-server.example.com",
    port=50001,
    user="db2inst1",
    password="password",
    ssl=True,
    ssl_server_certificate="/path/to/server.arm",
)
```

### `ibis.connect` URL format

In addition to `ibis.db2.connect`, you can also connect to Db2 by
passing a properly-formatted Db2 connection URL to `ibis.connect`:

```python
# Plain connection
con = ibis.connect(f"db2://{username}:{password}@{hostname}:{port}/{database}")

# SSL connection via URL query parameters
con = ibis.connect(f"db2://{username}:{password}@{hostname}:50001/{database}?ssl=true")

# SSL with server certificate
con = ibis.connect(
    f"db2://{username}:{password}@{hostname}:50001/{database}"
    "?ssl=true&ssl_server_certificate=/path/to/server.arm"
)
```

## Temporary tables require a USER TEMPORARY tablespace

`CREATE GLOBAL TEMPORARY TABLE` fails with `SQL0286N` unless the database has a
USER TEMPORARY tablespace whose page size is large enough for the table's rows.
A 32K page size is sufficient for the Ibis test suite. For example:

```sql
CREATE BUFFERPOOL IBIS_BP32K SIZE 250 PAGESIZE 32K;
CREATE USER TEMPORARY TABLESPACE IBIS_TEMP_4K PAGESIZE 4K
    MANAGED BY AUTOMATIC STORAGE;
CREATE USER TEMPORARY TABLESPACE IBIS_TEMP_32K PAGESIZE 32K
    MANAGED BY AUTOMATIC STORAGE BUFFERPOOL IBIS_BP32K;
```

Temporary tables are created with `ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS`, and the connection
runs with autocommit enabled.

## Overwriting tables

`create_table(..., overwrite=True)` **replaces the table**. The new table is
built under a temporary name first, so a query that fails leaves the existing
table as it was. After that the old table is dropped and the new one takes its
name. The replacement has only the columns of the new data: primary keys and
other constraints, indexes, triggers and grants on the old table are not
carried over. Recreate them after the overwrite, for example:

```python
con.create_table("t", new_data, overwrite=True)
con.raw_sql('ALTER TABLE "t" ADD PRIMARY KEY ("id")')
con.raw_sql('CREATE INDEX "t_ix" ON "t" ("name")')
```

To replace the rows and keep the table definition, use
`con.insert("t", new_data, overwrite=True)` instead. It truncates the table
first, so it must be the first statement of its unit of work.

Db2 cannot rename a temporary table, so with `temp=True` the new data is
copied into a re-created table. The query still runs before the old table is
touched, but the old temporary table is gone if that final copy fails.

## Existing connections and autocommit

`ibis.db2.connect` turns autocommit on. `Backend.from_connection` uses the
connection as it is and never commits for you. If the connection has autocommit
off, Ibis issues a warning, reads may hold locks, and changes (including
created tables) stay uncommitted and invisible to other connections until you
call `con.commit()`. Call `con.set_autocommit(True)` before passing the
connection in to avoid this.

## Db2 server versions

The backend is tested against Db2 12.1.5, which the test suite uses in CI.
The full test suite was also run against Db2 11.5.9: everything passes except
the 7 tests below, which need `ibis.uuid()`.

| Feature | Db2 12.1 | Db2 11.5 |
| ------- | -------- | -------- |
| `ibis.uuid()` | Works | Fails when executed with `SQL0440N`: the `GENERATE_UUID` function it uses does not exist before 12.1 |

On 11.5.9 these tests fail for that reason:
`test_uuid_function`, `test_uuid_unique_each_row`, the four `uuid` cases of
`test_impure_correlated`, `test_chained_selections`,
`test_impure_uncorrelated_same_id` and `test_impure_uncorrelated_different_id`,
and `test_self_join_with_generated_keys`. `pi` and casting strings to dates,
times and timestamps work on both versions.

## Limitations

- **Python UDFs**: Not currently supported
- **Streaming**: Not supported
- **Unsupported types**: Array, map, struct, JSON, null, and unsigned integer
  types raise `UnsupportedBackendType`, because Db2 has no equivalent.
  `XML` columns are reported with an `unknown` type.
- **Decimal precision**: Db2 allows at most 31 digits, so `decimal(38, 9)`
  isn't supported. The default `decimal` maps to `DECIMAL(31, 6)`.
- **Unsupported operations**: Operations with no Db2 equivalent (for example
  `ArgMin`, `ArgMax`, `Mode`, `First`, `Last`, `Kurtosis`, `Reverse`, `IsNan`,
  `Strftime`, and array and map operations) raise `OperationNotDefinedError`
  when compiled.
- **Whitespace stripping**: `strip`, `lstrip` and `rstrip` remove ASCII
  whitespace only. Unicode whitespace such as the non-breaking space is kept,
  which differs from pandas.
- **Ordered `group_concat`**: Passing `order_by` to `group_concat` raises
  `UnsupportedOperationError`, because Db2 rejects the `NULLS FIRST/LAST` that
  Ibis adds to the ordering.
- **Emoji**: `ibm_db` can segfault when fetching emoji characters, so avoid
  querying them with this backend. Characters outside the Basic Multilingual
  Plane (such as emoji) also corrupt the statement text when used in a SQL
  literal.
- **String length**: `string` columns map to `VARCHAR(32672)`, the longest
  `VARCHAR` Db2 allows. Longer values fail with `SQL0302N`.
- **NaN and infinity**: `DOUBLE` and `REAL` columns can't store `NaN` or
  infinity, so inserting them fails with `SQL0302N`.
- **Division by zero**: Dividing by zero raises `SQL0801N` instead of
  returning `NULL` or infinity.
- **Long literal aliases**: An unnamed string literal longer than about 120
  characters fails with `SQL0107N`, because its text becomes the column name.
  Give it a name with `.name(...)`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
BACKEND = "Db2"
```
